newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market erased morning's gains to end weaker on Wednesday, pulled lower by a negative trend in main foreign bonds markets, dealers said.
But traders added the negative close gave a good excuse to cash in some profits, after sharp gains in latest weeks.
"A consolidation was long overdue. And this is making our market even stronger," a dealer in Madrid said.
The 10-year spread versus Bunds, after a record low in the morning at 64 basis points, ended at 68 basis points with same analysts forecasting it could bounce back above the level of 70 basis points.
"There is still one year to go before the Maastricht's final exam. If the spread (over Bunds) should fall too quick, what remains to do for us?," a trader in Madrid asked.
But beside the possibility of technical falls, dealers said Spanish fundamentals were offering a very optimistic outlook.

Earlier on Wednesday the government published April budget deficit figure, which showed a sharp improvement versus March, with the deficit to GDP ratio falling to 0.7 percent versus 1.1 percent in the first three months.
And a few analysts are already looking forward for another fall in inflation, when May data comes out in June.
